action: Octopus advises customers to watch for unusual account activity, be wary of suspicious calls, messages, emails or links, and never share personal, account or verification information with anyone claiming to be Octopus.
date_note: The page, published 27 November, says the company reported the attack on Friday morning (27 November).

evidence.quote: the personal data of around 7,500 individual customers

exec: Octopus says around 7,500 customers and approximately 22,000 merchants are involved; a few functions may be temporarily affected as a precaution.
geo_basis: country: Octopus is Hong Kong's payment operator; the page gives no city
plain: Octopus says a cyberattack involved data of around 7,500 customers and approximately 22,000 merchants. It says credit card and bank account information are not involved and its main services operate normally.

sources.name: Octopus Cards: Notice of Information Security Incident (Chinese)
Eyoon Masr: a whole city's wallet in hackers' sights (Arabic)

summary: Octopus Cards says in its 27 November notice that it detected a cyberattack that morning and moved to contain it. It says around 7,500 customers and approximately 22,000 merchants are involved: customer names and photos, possibly some automatic top-up bank numbers and amounts, and merchant contact details. Octopus says credit card and bank account information are not involved and main services are operating normally.
title: Octopus reports cyberattack affecting around 7,500 customers and approximately 22,000 merchants

validation.note: Octopus own notice (27 Nov) read; The Standard (page shows no full date, '2 hours ago', breach detected 'on Friday'; dated 27 Nov) and Eyoon Masr (Arabic) relay it.

review.note: Compared date, 7,500/22,000 figures, data types, no card/bank data, advice against Octopus notice and The Standard
